title: An unreadable ancestor leaves higher ancestors selectable

codex.criterion: breaks a trust or confinement boundary
codex.failure_scenario: During cleanup, the factory cannot inspect its parent but can inspect a higher ancestor carrying the invocation marker. It treats that ancestor as an owned child and can terminate an unrelated runner or supervising process.

reproduction.output:
F1 Linux: grandparent excluded=false; selected=[424245]
F1 Darwin: grandparent excluded=false; selected=[424245,424243,424242]

codex.evidence: The probe bundled the actual HEAD scanners with synthetic filesystem and libproc backends; no real ancestor was signalled. Linux ancestry handles EACCES and other listed errors with `break` at line 57, then returns the incomplete `protectedPids`. Darwin does the same at processes-darwin.ts:125. Both scanners selected the readable, marked synthetic grandparent after its unreadable parent stopped the ancestry walk. Linux selection uses `if (carriesMarker(environment.split("\0"))) marked.push(Number(name));`; Darwin uses `marked.add(pid)` for a matching environment. proc.ts:245-266 then claims selected processes with readable birth identities and signals them; an ancestor's stable identity does not establish ownership. Base had no caller-ancestry exclusions, so this is an incomplete delivery of the requested protection rather than a newly introduced exposure.
codex.reason: The later commit makes both ancestry walkers throw on unreadable ancestors, preventing discovery and signalling from proceeding with an incomplete exclusion set.

opus.failure_scenario: No real process can hit this. Every invocation gets a new random marker, and the caller's ancestors started before that marker existed, so none of them can carry it. They also cannot be in the new child's own process group or session.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/f1.ts (calls linuxCallerAncestors with a stat reader that throws EACCES for process.ppid and would return a stat row for a grandparent 999001)
reproduction.output: ppid 50606 protected [ 1, 50675, 50606 ] grandparent protected? false

opus.evidence: The walk does stop at an unreadable ancestor (proc.ts:57-59: `if (["ENOENT","ESRCH","EACCES","EPERM"].includes(...)) break;`; processes-darwin.ts:125 does the same), so higher ancestors are left out of the protected set. That part is mechanically true. But nothing outside the protected set can select a real ancestor. (1) The marker is `randomUUID()`, created just before spawn (proc.ts:356-369), and environment only flows down to children, so no earlier ancestor can have `LIMITLESS_INVOCATION=<marker>` or `LIMITLESS_INVOCATION_<marker>=1`. agentEnv keeps only outer markers. (2) The Linux /proc scan and the ps path select by marker only (proc.ts:93-96, 141-147, 191-197). (3) On Darwin, group/session membership needs `leader.pid === group`, where group is the new detached child's pid. Ancestor-chain membership needs a marked parent. Hidden-orphan membership needs a birth time after the invocation and a cwd in the run's directories. An ancestor born before the spawn meets none of these. (4) An ENOENT means the parent exited mid-walk. The caller has then been reparented, so the old grandparent is no longer its ancestor, and it still lacks the marker. On Linux, /proc/<pid>/stat of a same-uid process is not EACCES even with hidepid. The reviewer's probe worked only because it fed the scanners synthetic data in which an ancestor carries the fresh marker, which cannot happen on a real machine.
opus.reason: The walk does stop early, but no real ancestor can carry the new per-invocation marker or meet Darwin's group, session or orphan rules, so nothing gets wrongly selected; c91310d makes the walk fail closed anyway.

opus.failure_scenario: Suppose a cancellation test is already failing, because the run never settles or a wait times out. Its cleanup then sends SIGKILL to every pid it saved earlier without checking that each is still the same process. If one of those pids has meanwhile been reused by another process on the shared machine, that unrelated process is killed.

opus.reason: The cleanup still sends SIGKILL to saved pids without checking identity when settlement fails, which the request ruled out; c91310d records each pid's birth time and signals only on a match (`killRetainedPids`).

codex.failure_scenario: The landing worker and a CI repair run operate on the same pull request. A pending merge completes at the older head after the repair pushes, leaving the repair outside the merged change and overwriting the repair's blocked land status.

reproduction.output: CI started with landState=waiting_ci, round status=queued, ghCalls=1. An explicit-SHA land request during a CI round returned queued. Held merge probe: merge pending=merging; delivery={state:blocked,pushedNewHead:true}; merge response={state:landed,reason:"merged 6c1851ffe79b"}. All three probes passed.

codex.evidence: HEAD's startRoundTrigger checks 'round in flight' and the CI cap but never active land entries. createLandEntry likewise inserts without checking rounds, and LandQueue.approval returns an explicit matching SHA without consulting approval staleness. Delivery updates active entries to blocked and aborts their workers, but queue.ts:575-592 awaits mergePullRequest and then calls landed without checking cancellation or current state. The reproduction used real local delivery and a deferred fake merge response; no GitHub request occurred. Base had no CI rounds or CI-delivery abort subscription, so this change introduces the competing CI path.
codex.reason: The later commit adds transactional exclusion at CI start and land insertion, checks readiness before live lookup without consuming attempts, skips known closed or merged PRs, rechecks rounds before merging, and removes active-entry rewriting and the abort subscription.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: A PR is in the land queue (queued, checking, waiting for CI, or merging) when its CI failure is classified. A CI fix round starts anyway, and the two then race. Its delivery forcibly marks the queue entry blocked, while a merge already in progress can still finish and record the entry as landed at the old head. The pushed fix then sits on a PR that was merged without it.

reproduction.output:
ADJ queued ["ci"] queued
ADJ checking ["ci"] checking
ADJ waiting_ci ["ci"] waiting_ci
ADJ merging ["ci"] merging   (a CI round started while each active land entry existed; expected 0 rounds). The held-merge interleaving (merge response pending while delivery pushes) is unreproduced: it needs a real in-flight GitHub merge.

opus.evidence: startRoundTrigger (store.ts 1195-1330) checks only 'round in flight' among review_rounds and never reads land_entries. markRoundDelivered for kind ci (store.ts 1378-1383): `UPDATE land_entries SET state = 'blocked' ... WHERE pr_url = ? AND state IN ('queued','checking','waiting_ci','merging','blocked')`. queue.ts 286-293 aborts the worker only through an in-process feed subscription. queue.ts merge() (561-592) calls landed() after mergePullRequest returns, and landed()/finish() (363-366, 703-706) write state 'landed' by id with no re-check. LandQueue.request (169-200) has no check for an in-flight round. All of this is new in base..head.
opus.reason: Head lets a CI round start and deliver while a land entry is active, then reconciles only through an in-process abort plus a state overwrite that a finishing merge can itself overwrite; 1f93323 adds ciFixTriggerReady, assertNoRoundInFlight on request/create/merge, and removes the abort subscription and the active-entry rewrite.

title: A pending CI trigger ignores a default branch that went red after it was recorded

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: A CI failure queues a repair while the default branch is green. The same check subsequently fails on the default branch, but processing the pending trigger still starts a repair against the pull request.

reproduction.output: After classifying first with main green and then with main red: persisted main state={"test":{"red":true,"episode":1}}. Processing triggers produced [{"state":"started","reason":null}] and rounds=1. Probe passed.

codex.evidence: HEAD's classifier records a trigger only under '!state.get(f.check)?.red' and persists current default-branch episodes with 'store.setSetting(`ci.main:${pr.repo}`, Object.fromEntries(state))'. However, startRoundTrigger's CI branch checks only 'ciRounds.length >= 2'; it never reads those episodes before inserting a round. Base already persisted the episodes but had no CI repair trigger path.
codex.reason: The later commit reads the classifier's persisted episode for the trigger's check during startRoundTrigger and skips it with 'default branch red' when appropriate.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: A PR's check fails while main is still green, so a CI fix trigger is recorded. Main then goes red on the same check before the next trigger pass, and the factory still starts a paid fix round for a failure that is really main's.

reproduction.command: head code in a $TMPDIR copy with 1f93323's test file; bun test test/ci-fix-rounds.test.ts (test 'pending CI trigger re-checks a default branch that went red')
reproduction.output: expect(factory.store.reviewRounds(url)).toHaveLength(0) -> Expected length: 0, Received length: 1

opus.evidence: ci-classifier.ts 199-200: `if (kind === "ci.needs_fix" && !repository && !unsafe && !state.get(f.check)?.red) store.recordCiFixTrigger(...)`. The main-red check runs only at record time. startRoundTrigger (store.ts 1195+) never reads ci.main:<repo>, and the poller's tick runs processConflictTriggers before observe(). The window is roughly one poll interval, or longer while lookups back off, so it is a narrow timing window rather than the ordinary path. That is why this is rated minor.
opus.reason: The default-branch-red exclusion is checked only when the trigger is recorded, never when it starts; 1f93323 re-reads ci.main:<repo> in startRoundTrigger and skips with 'default branch red'.

reproduction.command: head code in a $TMPDIR copy with 1f93323's test file; bun test test/ci-fix-rounds.test.ts (test 'a stop-only CI implementation ends needs_human after one invocation')

title: OPERATIONS conflates routing exhaustion with provider contention

codex.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
codex.failure_scenario: An operator sees all provider slots occupied and consults the troubleshooting table. They incorrectly expect the run to stop for human intervention while it is actually waiting for a slot.

reproduction.output:
F2 while busy: {"status":"running","settled":false,"calls":0,"wait":"waiting for alpha slot (0 ahead), up to unbounded"}
F2 after release: {"settled":true,"calls":1}

codex.evidence: The offline probe saturated a fake provider, invoked RunContext.invoke, observed the pending invocation, then released the slot. At head, src/pipeline/context.ts:525–539 throws NoCapacityError when no eligible target exists; lines 541–578 instead wait for admission when providers are busy. Engine lines 275 and 345 map NoCapacityError to needs_human. Waiting can eventually exhaust an invocation deadline, but contention does not immediately end the run. OPERATIONS states `No provider capacity ends a run needs_human` without this distinction. Base instead listed `concurrency limit, or no provider available` as queued causes; the inaccurate blanket statement is new.
codex.reason: The later commit explicitly distinguishes exhausted routing candidates from busy provider slots and explains the invocation-deadline qualification.

opus.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: An operator reads that no provider capacity ends a run as needs_human. When every eligible provider is just busy, the run actually stays running and waits for a slot, so the operator may think something is wrong, or wrongly expect the run to have ended.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: docs-only claim; checked by reading the routing code in src/pipeline/context.ts
opus.evidence: At head, the OPERATIONS.md troubleshooting row says: "No provider capacity ends a run `needs_human`, rather than leaving it queued." In context.ts (~525-539), `if (!target) { ... throw new NoCapacityError(...) }` applies only when no candidate is eligible. engine.ts:275 maps NoCapacityError to needs_human. When candidates exist but are busy, context.ts (~541-578) waits for a slot instead (`// With no alternative left, contention waits until a slot opens or the invocation deadline`, `tracker.acquire/acquireFirst`, log `waiting for ${provider} slot`). So 'no capacity → needs_human' is true for routing exhaustion but not for slot contention. The part about runs not staying `queued` is correct.
opus.reason: The sentence lumps routing exhaustion (which ends the run needs_human) together with busy slots (where the run waits while running); 93bee29 rewrites it to separate the two.

title: Private literals found by verify are missing from the change view's catalogue

codex.failure_scenario: Verification discovers a private runtime value and withholds it from public feedback. If that value also appears in the change or report, an agent can retrieve it through the change view.

reproduction.output: F2: publicText="Observed '[private detail]' during verification. [1 private details withheld]"; ownerOnlyRows={"n":1}; available=true; patch contained "+runtimeProbeSecret\n"; report="Observed 'runtimeProbeSecret' during verification."

codex.evidence: The probe persisted verifier evidence and an owner-only diagnostic associated with a verify invocation. HEAD builds its catalogue only with privateHoldoutDetails(holdout, publicSources), omitting the optional observed argument and never reading verifier observations. In contrast, context.ts invokes redactHoldoutText(value, holdout, publicSources), which harvests observed literals by default, and records the raw diagnostic separately. Base already performed that observed-literal redaction; the new endpoint introduces an output path that fails to preserve it. The endpoint did not directly return owner-only rows, but returned the same protected value from the patch and report.
codex.reason: The later commit harvests private observations from persisted verification results and relevant owner-only verifier diagnostics as internal catalogue inputs without returning those rows.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: During verification the verifier notices a value such as 'runtimeProbeSecret'. The factory hides that value in its own verification copies, but the change view still shows it wherever it appears in the patch or the report. In practice the value only gets there when it is already in the implementer's own code or in public acceptance evidence that the factory's report already prints, so little new information leaks.

reproduction.command: bun test $SCRATCH/repro.test.ts (case 'F2 verifier literal': run state lastVerify H-1 evidence "Observed 'runtimeProbeSecret' during verification.", the literal in probe.ts and in report.md)
reproduction.output: F2 diff: "...+export const runtimeProbeSecret = 1;\n" report: Implementer saw runtimeProbeSecret

opus.evidence: mcp-change.ts:107 calls `privateHoldoutDetails(holdout, publicSources)` without the `observed` argument, so only authored scenario details are protected. The pipeline's redactHoldoutText (context.ts:709, verification.ts:30-35) also collects literals observed in verifier text. The request asks that nothing the factory withholds from agents appears in the view. Why minor: the report's holdout section is dropped completely (withoutHoldoutSection), and public-row evidence is already published unredacted by report.ts, so the literal reaches the view only through text the factory or the implementer already exposes.
opus.reason: bcea6cd3 adds verifier notes, evidence, gate citations and owner diagnostics to the protected set.

title: Status and the change view can serve a head the factory has already superseded

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: The factory records a newly pushed head before its polling snapshot refreshes. An agent is instructed to review the previous head and receives its change view, then has that review rejected because the PR has moved.

reproduction.output: F3: recordedHead.sha="247d2e8a0261da3b5372d351b953193b2a72ae25"; snapshotHead="56367b7c9ec488c5431bc3906c18179e3de161ef". Status returned state="Review needed" and headSha="56367b7c9ec488c5431bc3906c18179e3de161ef". Change returned available=true with that old SHA. Review submission using fake gh rejected it: "head moved: the PR is at 247d2e8a0261da3b5372d351b953193b2a72ae25, not the reviewed 56367b7c9ec488c5431bc3906c18179e3de161ef".

codex.evidence: The probe used the real Store, getChange, status schema/explanation, and submitReview with an injected fake GitHub response. Status derives its advertised SHA solely from commitSha.safeParse(pr?.headRefOid). getChange similarly uses snapshot.data.headRefOid and rechecks only githubPrData after awaited Git reads. Neither consults prHead or push state, although submitReview uses the recorded head version and observePrHead's concurrency check. Base did not advertise a concrete review SHA or expose this change view; those new outputs introduce the demonstrated stale-head behavior.
codex.reason: The later commit shares a validator that rejects snapshot/recorded-head disagreement and active pushes, checks the head epoch after Git reads, and refreshes status detail after its awaited land query.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: A review round pushes a new head and the factory records it, but the GitHub poll has not refreshed yet. Status tells the agent to review the old commit, and the change view serves that old diff as available. The agent reviews the wrong code and its submission is then refused as 'head moved'. This can last a whole poll interval on installations without webhooks.

reproduction.output: F3 status: {"state":"Review needed","nextAction":"...review PR head 99fac1c1... (base)","headSha":"99fac1c1...","latestRound":{..."deliveredSha":"99062e6b..."}} recorded: {"sha":"99062e6b...","version":2}; F3 view: true 99fac1c1... (old head)

opus.evidence: mcp-status.ts:56-57 takes headSha only from `pr?.headRefOid`, the github_prs snapshot. mcp-change.ts:83 and 229-231 also use only store.githubPrData. Round pushes write pr_heads (beginPrPush/endPrPush) but not github_prs, and review submission refuses a SHA that no longer matches (review-round.ts:190-193). Status's own latestRound.deliveredSha therefore disagrees with the head it asks the agent to review, which contradicts the requirement that status on a run with a delivered round names that round's head.
opus.reason: bcea6cd3 adds reviewableHead, which compares the snapshot with pr_heads and the pushing flag, and returns 'superseded' in both tools.

title: Git config can hide changed submodules

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: A repository has Git configured to ignore submodule differences, and a PR changes a submodule revision. The agent receives an available change view with that change omitted, leaving its code review incomplete.

reproduction.output: {"claim":"F4","available":true,"files":[],"patch":"","explicitNumstat":"1\t1\tmodule\u0000"}

codex.evidence: The probe constructed an isolated repository with a committed gitlink revision change and diff.ignoreSubmodules=all. HEAD's real getChange returned an empty file list. Running the hardened Git wrapper against the same commits with --ignore-submodules=none returned the gitlink as changed. The listing command is git diff --no-renames --numstat -z ..., and the patch command likewise omits --ignore-submodules=none. worktreeGit pins diff.submodule=short, which controls presentation rather than overriding ignoreSubmodules. Base had no change-view endpoint. Rename behavior is already pinned with --no-renames; the demonstrated omission concerns submodules.
codex.reason: The later commit explicitly adds --ignore-submodules=none to both the changed-file listing and per-file patch commands.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: On a machine whose git config sets diff.ignoreSubmodules=all (for example in a global gitconfig), a change that moves a submodule pointer disappears from the change view's file list, which still reports the view as complete. reproduction.output:
F4 default files: ["hello.txt","submod"]

AGENTS.md: 'Git is configurable. Set the options you depend on explicitly.' Minor because it needs a non-default config, and the deterministic audit blocks submodule changes unless they are explicitly allowed.
opus.reason: bcea6cd3 adds --ignore-submodules=none to both the numstat and patch git diff calls.

title: Cached gate results and stored handles are reused without checking the commit they ran on

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: A checkout changes while the daemon is stopped during post-merge checks. After restarting, the factory can accept the newer commit using the previous commit's passing results.

reproduction.output: F1 {"cached":{"currentSha":"M2","recordedSha":"M1","starts":1,"attaches":1},"pending":{"starts":0,"attaches":1,"currentSha":"M2"}}

codex.evidence: The isolated probe mocked headSha and injected an executor; it reproduced both reuse mechanisms, not publication. HEAD returns `results[purpose]` immediately and selects a pending handle using only stage, round and purpose. Neither path compares commits. Delivery's validateMerge checks parents, not equality with the tested commit, and its rebase checks lack the ordinary gate-evidence SHA guard. At base, mergeForDelivery called runGates afresh rather than reusing persisted results.
codex.reason: The response removes completed-result caching and requires pending.sha to equal the current checkout SHA before attaching.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: If the checked-out commit changes between the moment a gate result is saved and the moment the daemon resumes (for example a gate script amends HEAD), the resumed rebase stage reuses the old commit's saved result and publishes the new commit without gating it. With today's local executor, an attached handle re-runs on the current tree, so only the saved-result path is exposed. A future remote executor would also return the old commit's result from a stored handle.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: needs a full engine restart harness with the checkout moved between checkpoints; judged from code
opus.evidence: gate-execution.ts:20-23 `if (ctx.state.gateResults?.stage !== stage || ...round !== round) ctx.state.gateResults = { stage, round, sha: await headSha(cwd), values: {} }; ... if (results[purpose]) return results[purpose];` The stored sha is never compared with the current head. Lines 25-28 pick the stored handle by stage, round and purpose only. In mergeForDelivery (engine.ts:2381-2396), a resume skips completeMerge when head != before and calls runGateExecution('rebase'). Nothing pins the head there. In normal operation nothing moves HEAD between the checkpoint and the resume (prepareMerge returns early and checkoutCommitted resets to HEAD). So it takes a gate or an outside actor moving HEAD, which base also didn't guard during an uninterrupted run.
opus.reason: The later commit drops the result cache and only reattaches a stored handle when `pending.sha === sha` for the current head.

title: A restart during a pending retry replays it without the setup it depends on

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts during a retry after setup installed dependencies. Resume removes those dependencies, skips the cached initial attempt and runs the retry without reinstalling them, incorrectly reporting a regression.

reproduction.output: F2 {"uninterrupted":"flaky","resumed":"regressed","output":"missing-setup","storedSetup":[]}

codex.evidence: The probe used real local setup/check commands with a fake confinement backend, simulated interruption at retry persistence, and removed the temporary dependency directory to model checkoutCommitted. HEAD calls `checkoutCommitted` before fetching the cached initial result; retryRegressions submits `{ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected }`. Thus setup is skipped after cleanup. Base also cleaned the checkout, but then reran runGates with the complete configuration, including setup.
codex.reason: The response removes completed-result caching and discards pending later attempts so resume reruns the initial suite and its setup.

opus.criterion: a resume/restart path repeats or loses work
opus.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a flaky check is being retried. On resume the factory wipes ignored files such as installed dependencies, skips setup by reusing the saved first result, and replays the retry without setup. The check fails for lack of dependencies, gets recorded as a blocking regression, and costs the run an extra implementation round.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: needs a daemon kill at the retry checkpoint and a real setup step; traced from code
opus.evidence: run.ts:283 `const retried = await runner({ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected });` On resume, engine.ts:1156 runs `checkoutCommitted(cwd, ...)`, which runs `git clean -ffdxq` (repos.ts:476) and removes ignored dependencies. Then `runGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", ...)` returns the cached `results.initial` (gate-execution.ts:23) without running setup, and the stored 'regression-retry' handle replays its saved request, which has `setup: []`. At base the whole stage, setup included, re-ran on resume. Baseline retries in prepare have the same exposure.
opus.reason: The later commit removes the result cache and only resumes 'baseline', 'initial' or 'rebase' handles, so a resumed stage starts over with setup.

title: Gate hooks reach only the local executor; an injected executor's events are dropped

codex.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
codex.failure_scenario: An injected executor provides check events, but the factory never reads them. Users lose per-check progress and landing logs even though the final result still determines success or failure.

reproduction.output: F3 {"emittedChecksAvailable":1,"consumed":0,"onResultCalls":0}

codex.evidence: The injected executor exposed an event iterator containing a check result; executeGate never entered it. HEAD supplies hooks only when constructing `localExecutor(hooks)` and then merely `return await execution.result`. An injected executor receives neither hooks nor an event consumer. Base passed hooks directly into runGates. The defect exists at the injectable seam, while default local execution remains observable.
codex.reason: The response consumes execution events centrally, includes setup phases, and passes slot hooks to attach.

opus.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: When a gate executor other than the built-in local one is plugged in, per-check results never reach the run's gate events or the landing queue's log file, and the wait and holder information for the gate slot is dropped. Production uses only the local executor today, so nothing visible breaks yet.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: no production path injects a non-local executor; shown from code
opus.evidence: executor.ts:124-127 `const executor = stored?.kind === "local" && injected?.kind !== "local" ? localExecutor(hooks) : (injected ?? localExecutor(hooks));` The hooks reach only localExecutor. executeGate only awaits `execution.result` and never iterates `execution.events`. The land queue's `onResult` appendFileSync (queue.ts:397) and the engine's gate events would therefore never fire for an injected executor.
opus.reason: executeGate now consumes `execution.events` and calls `hooks.onResult` for both setup and check results, and the local executor no longer calls the hook directly.

title: A failed execution leaves its handle stored for the next attempt

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An execution fails because of a temporary infrastructure problem. Retrying with the same executor can repeatedly retrieve the completed failure instead of starting another attempt after the problem is resolved.

reproduction.output:
F5 {"starts":1,"attaches":2,"pendingHandleRetained":true}
F5-local {"verifications":1,"errors":["one-time infrastructure failure","one-time infrastructure failure"],"pendingHandleRetained":true}

codex.evidence: The first probe used a rejecting injected executor. A second used the actual reusable localExecutor with confinement verification configured to fail only once: the second attempt never reached verification and returned the cached rejection. HEAD clears gateExecution only on success; its catch simply rethrows. localExecutor retains completed executions in its map and returns them on attach. Default non-injected local execution constructs a fresh executor and therefore avoids this particular repeated-failure consequence. Base had no durable execution handle to retain.
codex.reason: The response clears and saves settled handles on failure as well as success, and removes settled local executions from its maps.

opus.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: A gate execution that ends in an error leaves its record marked as still in progress. When the same stage runs again, the factory attaches to that old execution instead of starting a fresh one. With the local executor this re-runs the saved (redacted) request and skips the baseline cache in prepare. A remote executor would hand back the same failure again.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: traced from code
opus.evidence: gate-execution.ts:53-56 `} catch (error) { ctx.checkCancelled(); throw error; }` never clears `ctx.state.gateExecution`, which is only cleared on success (line 51). Lines 24-28 then reuse it on the next matching attempt, and engine.ts:506 treats `gateExecution?.stage === "prepare"` as a reason to skip the baseline cache.

title: A slow but answering lease service is still treated as unreachable, so the command runs unslotted

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: An agent requests permission to run tests while the daemon is responding slowly. The wrapper starts the tests without permission, allowing them to compete with suites that already hold the available slots.

reproduction.output: Fake transports and virtual clock: HTTP busy response delayed 1300ms plus socket refusal caused the work callback to start at 1000ms of a 5000ms budget; the valid late busy response subsequently arrived. With every busy response delayed 2400ms, work started at 31900ms of a 60000ms budget after 13 valid late busy responses. Both cases warned that the daemon was unreachable.

codex.evidence: HEAD's wrapper first uses `bounded(..., 1000)`, then executes `const reply = await second(body, signal)` after any non-LeaseRejected error. A socket refusal therefore replaces the HTTP timeout. In gate-slot.ts, `(first && !(e instanceof DaemonTimeoutError))` classifies that replacement as unreachable, and the outer catch warns before executing work. Independently, `lastReply = clock.now()` runs only after a timely request result, so late replies cannot prevent the 30000ms silence fallback. Base already had the silence rule, but had neither this wrapper nor its timeout-masking transport fallback. The later commit preserves DaemonTimeoutError across fallback, observes late replies, and disables silence-based unslotted execution for agent commands.
codex.reason: Both reported fail-open paths reproduced at HEAD, and the later commit directly addresses their error classification and timeout handling.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: When the daemon is slow rather than down, an agent's test command can skip the queue and run alongside a full gate suite. That happens if the HTTP reply takes over 1 s and the scratch socket can't be reached, or if every reply takes over 2 s for 30 s. The cost is CPU contention under load, which is the situation slotting exists to prevent; no state is lost.

title: A delayed recovery reply stops heartbeats while the work keeps running

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: A running test suite renews its expired reservation, but the renewal response is delayed. Retries stop maintaining the replacement reservation, allowing another suite to start while the first suite is still running.

reproduction.output: Using the real AgentTestSession and Semaphore with fake time: at 34000ms the delayed replacement lease was adopted, occupancy was 1, and work remained running; warnings included the recovery timeout and rejected retry. At 62000ms occupancy had fallen to 0 while the first work remained running, and a second invocation acquired the lane.

codex.evidence: HEAD marks the old lease `previous.status = "recovered"` before returning its replacement, but recovery requires `previous.status !== "heartbeat"` to be false. Retrying the old lease therefore rejects. The wrapper's catch schedules another heartbeat only when `!(opts.agentTest && e instanceof LeaseRejected)`, so this rejection stops renewal. A late reply still updates the lease ID, but that adoption does not restart heartbeats. Base had no AgentTestSession recovery restriction, and its heartbeat catch unconditionally retried while work remained active. The later commit records the replacement registration for idempotent recovery retries and calls `beat()` when adopting a recovery response.
codex.reason: The delayed-recovery sequence reproduced premature capacity release, and the later commit fixes both non-idempotent recovery and heartbeat restart.

codex.failure_scenario: An owner submits a substantial review that fits the accepted input limits. The factory pushes the fixes but sends an oversized comment, so GitHub rejects the evidence publication and delivery remains incomplete.

reproduction.output: Twenty findings with 20,000-character details were accepted with HTTP 201. F3 {"status":"needs_human","commentCharacters":404217,"pushed":true,"comments":0}. Fake gh rejected comments exceeding 65,536 characters; real GitHub rejection was not exercised because network access was prohibited.

codex.evidence: Head appends `(blocked ? `\n\n${buildReport(ctx, false)}` : "")` and sends the result directly through `gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, text)`. renderReport includes the complete request, which contains quoted review details. ReviewVerdictSchema accepts up to 50 findings with details up to 20,000 characters each. checkPublication checks private strings and repository content, without limiting length. Base review delivery used roundSection, which includes finding titles and locations rather than the full quoted request. The later commit replaces the appended report with blocked evidence and a report link, redacts before truncating, and caps the comment at 60,000 characters.
codex.reason: Accepted review input produces an oversized outbound comment, and the later commit directly bounds that payload.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: A review round with very long reviewer findings ends blocked by the environment. Its commit is pushed, but the evidence comment is larger than GitHub's 65,536-character limit, so GitHub rejects it and the PR never shows the blocked-criteria evidence. Every resume tries the same oversized comment and fails again.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/size.ts  (calls renderReport with prompt = reviewRoundPrompt(original request of ~3.4k chars, 10 findings x 8,000-char detail))
reproduction.output: report chars 84939 > 65536: true

opus.evidence: engine.ts:2021-2030 appends `(blocked ? `\n\n${buildReport(ctx, false)}` : "")` to the comment with no size limit. renderReport quotes the whole prompt (report.ts:80-84), and a round prompt carries the original request plus up to 50 findings of up to 20,000 characters each (review-round.ts:15-28, 57-67). checkPublication checks privacy only. The push and markRoundDelivered/save('round-delivered') happen before the comment, so the commit still reaches the PR. Only the evidence comment is lost, and the catch block logs 'Could not open draft PR'.
opus.reason: Above about 60k characters of finding text the new comment is rejected after the push, losing the evidence (diagnostic only); the later commit posts bounded 🚧 rows, cut to 60,000 characters, with a link to the full report.

title: Redacting the whole run state on every save changes what a resumed run executes and compares

codex.criterion: loses or corrupts persisted state
codex.failure_scenario: An operator runs a check whose command contains a registered credential or a literal terminal escape sequence. Saving the run rewrites that command and comparison inputs, so a resumed run can fail a previously passing check or report an unchanged script as changed.

reproduction.output:
{"claim":"F1","label":"credential","liveCommandPreserved":true,"savedCommandPreserved":false,"uninterrupted":true,"restarted":false,"unchangedScriptEqualsSaved":false,"cacheableRaw":true,"cacheableRedacted":false}
{"claim":"F1","label":"escape","liveCommandPreserved":true,"savedCommandPreserved":false,"uninterrupted":true,"restarted":false,"unchangedScriptEqualsSaved":false,"cacheableRaw":true,"cacheableRedacted":false}

codex.evidence: The temporary probe exercised RunContext.save(), SQLite persistence, reconstruction of RunContext, and real local shell checks with an injected confinement backend; it required neither network nor real Seatbelt. At head, save() writes `this.store.setRunState(this.run.id, redactGateData(this.state));`; base writes `this.store.setRunState(this.run.id, this.state);`. redactGateData transforms every string using credential replacement and terminal-control stripping, including gatesConfig and baselineScripts. Head also newly stores `redactGateData(fresh)` in the baseline cache, while cacheableBaseline requires `c.command === cfg.checks[i]?.run`. Attribution caveat: both base and head already call `this.state = redactGateData(this.state)` in the constructor, so restart divergence alone is preexisting evidence, not proof of an introduced regression. The newly introduced defects are destructive save-time persistence and cache-command mutation. The response restores literal save/cache writes and also removes constructor-wide sanitization. The claim's specific performance numbers were not independently verified.
codex.reason: The new save and cache transformations corrupt operational inputs, and the response removes both mechanisms, although related load-time corruption already existed at base.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: If a gate command contains a registered secret or a terminal escape sequence and the daemon restarts in the middle of the gates stage, the resumed run executes and compares the cleaned-up command instead of the real one, so it can reach a different verdict. The base release already did this when it loaded run state; the only new cost here is that such a baseline is cached in cleaned-up form, so it never matches and is simply run again.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/r.ts  (calls redactGateData on a state whose gatesConfig check runs printf '\x1b[31mred', then applies it a second time)
reproduction.output:
"printf '\u001b[31mred'" -> "printf 'red'"
idempotent: true

opus.evidence: The resume divergence is real at head but not introduced by it. At base, the RunContext constructor already redacted the whole loaded state: `git show af76c2be:src/pipeline/context.ts` line 307 reads `this.state = redactGateData(this.state);`, and head keeps it at context.ts:310. So at base a resumed run loaded the raw state and redacted it. At head it loads state that was redacted on save and redacts it again. redactGateData is idempotent (repro above), so a resumed run ends up with the same redacted gatesConfig, spec and holdout either way. The head line `this.store.setRunState(this.run.id, redactGateData(this.state))` (context.ts:373) therefore does not change what a resumed run executes; the claim misattributes the mechanism. On an uninterrupted run, head also adds `ctx.state.baseline = redactGateData(...)` (engine.ts:530) and `cmp = redactGateData(cmp)` (engine.ts:1207). compareGates pairs baseline and after results by name (`baseline?.checks.find((b) => b.name === r.name)`, run.ts:249), so neither changes an uninterrupted verdict. What head does introduce is `store.putBaselineCache(key, redactGateData(fresh), ...)` (engine.ts:516). cacheableBaseline compares `c.command === cfg.checks[i]?.run` exactly (cache.ts:158), so such an entry never hits and the baseline is re-run. That costs performance only, plus an extra stringify and parse on every save. The full engine restart scenario was not re-run here; it rests on the quoted code.
opus.reason: 13a7b2e1 removes both the constructor redaction (the actual pre-existing source of the resume divergence) and the save-time redaction, and stores the baseline cache entry unredacted again.

title: Local gate work can keep running after its execution is forgotten

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: A landing log write fails while checks are running, or the engine replaces a stored execution belonging to another purpose or commit. The original check continues after its handle is forgotten, consuming a gate slot and running alongside replacement work.
codex.evidence: The temporary probe used localExecutor and runGateExecution with real shell children, recording each child's own PID. A throwing onResult hook rejected the wrapper, cleared persisted gateExecution, and allowed replacement work to finish while the original child remained alive. A separate live execution with a mismatched stored purpose/SHA likewise survived replacement. Explicit cancellation and awaiting each original result stopped the children and released their slots. At head, `await Promise.all([execution.result, events])` rejects when event forwarding throws, but finally only invokes onSettled, removes the abort listener, and awaits `cancellation`, which remains undefined without an abort. gate-execution.ts:59-64 then clears the handle. Its lines 29-32 also discard mismatched handles without cancellation. At base, hooks ran synchronously inside the gate loop; a throwing hook unwound that loop and released its slot before subsequent checks started. The response adds cancellation on errors, awaits execution.result before onSettled, tracks live executions, and cancels/awaits a mismatched live handle before clearing it.
codex.reason: Both claimed orphan-work paths reproduced at head, and the response adds cancellation and settlement before forgetting the execution.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: If writing a check's result fails (for example the land queue's log append or an event-store write), the gate stage reports an error, but the remaining gate checks keep running in the background. They keep using the shared gate slot and CPU, and a retry can end up waiting behind them.

reproduction.command: cd $TMPDIR/adj && bun f2.ts  (runs executeGate with checks [a: true, b: 'sleep 2; touch marker'] and an onResult hook that throws; waits 4s, then checks for the marker)
reproduction.output:
rejected: log write failed t= 1793363378549
second check ran after rejection: true

opus.evidence: At base, run.ts runAll called the hook inline inside the loop (`const r = await runOne(c, cwd, signal); checks.push(r); onResult?.(r, "check");`). A throwing hook therefore rejected runLocalGates itself: the loop stopped, the slot was released and no later check started. At head the local executor pushes results into a queue, and executeGate (executor.ts:160-172) forwards them in a separate task: `const events = (async () => { for await (const event of execution.events) if (event.type === "check") hooks.onResult?.(...) })(); const [result] = await Promise.all([execution.result, events]); return result; } finally { onSettled(); signal.removeEventListener("abort", abort); await cancellation; }`. When the forwarder rejects, there is no catch that cancels, so runLocalGates keeps going, as the repro confirms. runGateExecution then clears the stored handle because onSettled ran. The reviewer's second path, a discarded handle that is still live in this process, is hard to reach at head, because onSettled fires in `finally` once the execution is attached and the handle is cleared. Path (1) carries the verdict.
opus.reason: 13a7b2e1 adds `catch (error) { abort(); throw error; }`, awaits `execution.result` in `finally` before onSettled, and cancels a live execution through cancelGateExecution before discarding a stored handle.

title: When the catalogue key can't be computed, the final freshness check is skipped and newly private text can be returned

codex.criterion: leaks a secret or private data
codex.failure_scenario: An agent requests a change view while the privacy freshness lookup fails. A verifier records a new private observation during Git inspection, and the response exposes that observation in the report.

reproduction.output: Using a real in-memory Store and mocked Git reads, injected failure of PRAGMA data_version and appended a verifier diagnostic during the first Git await. Response: available=true; reports[0].text="Report includes fallbackRaceSecret." A subsequent read with normal key computation did not expose fallbackRaceSecret. Test passed.

When key is null, that final guard never executes. The reproduction confirms that the rebuilt catalogue becomes stale and the final privateOutputData pass does not independently protect new holdout-derived literals. This change-view module and its fallback path do not exist at base.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle

If a verifier diagnostic with new holdout text is written while git runs, the view is returned without the final staleness check and can show that newly private text to the agent.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: forcing the fingerprint function to fail needs it to be injected or a SQLite read to throw. Every run named in a review round always exists (the rounds query joins runs, and runs are never deleted), so null only comes from the exception path. The guard below is unambiguous in the code.
opus.evidence: Line 391: `const key = catalogueKey(...)` returns null from its catch ('the caller rebuilds rather than reusing patterns'). The catalogue is built once, before the git awaits at lines 402-450. The only re-check after those awaits, at line 488, is `if (key && catalogueKey(...) !== key) return {available:false...}`, so a null key skips it and the function returns content redacted against a catalogue built before the awaits. This fails open, which goes against the 'fail closed' rule. Getting a null key needs an exception from SQLite, JSON or the private-strings read, which is rare in normal operation.
opus.reason: The later commit changes the guard to `if (!key || catalogueKey(...) !== key)`, so a missing key now refuses.

title: A whitespace pattern built from holdout text scans quadratically

codex.criterion: stops the factory or the running release from working
codex.failure_scenario: An agent opens a change containing a long whitespace line while a private check contains a quoted tab followed by a letter. Redaction monopolizes the daemon's execution thread, delaying other requests and factory progress; larger inputs extend the stall quadratically.

reproduction.output: Through HEAD getChange with mocked Git, holdout description `Check output.\nIt contains "\tZ".` and an added line of spaces ending in Y: 32768 spaces => 408 ms wall / 410 ms CPU; 65536 => 1621 / 1619 ms; 131072 => 6449 / 6448 ms. Each response was available=true and returned only 16000 diff characters. Test passed.

codex.evidence: HEAD constructs multiline patterns with `.replace(/\s+/gu, "\\s+")`, producing an unanchored whitespace repetition before the required letter. `redactMultiline` scans complete content using `text.matchAll(pattern)` before paging. Doubling the input produced approximately four times the CPU cost, confirming quadratic scanning rather than exponential backtracking. This matching path is absent at base. The synchronous scan blocks the shared daemon thread and has no cancellation check or input-size bound.
codex.reason: The later commit collapses whitespace in both the scanned text and private details before literal matching, removing the repeated whitespace regex mechanism.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle

A change-view request then spends seconds of CPU in one regex scan (6 s at 128K characters, growing with the square of the length) and blocks the daemon's event loop.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/f2.ts  (builds the pattern exactly as at lines 310-314 from the detail "\tZ" and runs matchAll over N spaces followed by 'Y')

A detail that starts with whitespace gives a leading `\s+`, and matchAll retries it at every position of a whitespace run. title: The catalogue cache has no size bound

codex.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
codex.failure_scenario: An agent opens a run with unusually large private diagnostics. Its generated matching catalogue remains in daemon memory after the request, retaining memory proportional to that run's private text until replacement or store collection.

reproduction.output: Created 128 distinct private literals in verifier diagnostics totaling 527634 characters. Both change reads returned available=true. Full diagnostic reads after the first request: 1; after the second: 1, confirming reuse of the large cached catalogue. Test passed; no daemon exhaustion was demonstrated.

codex.evidence: HEAD declares `const catalogues = new WeakMap<Factory["store"], { key: string; redact: HoldoutRedactor }>()` and unconditionally caches any successfully keyed catalogue with `if (key) catalogues.set(store, { key, redact: holdoutRedact })`. The retained closure references compiled patterns and distinctive-detail strings assembled without a character or pattern-count limit. Weak keys allow collection when a Store dies, but do not bound the catalogue retained for the long-lived daemon Store. This cache is absent at base. The demonstrated consequence is excess retention, not a proven crash.
codex.reason: The later commit limits cache eligibility to 2048 details and 256000 UTF-16 characters, and deletes the cached entry when a catalogue exceeds either limit.

opus.reproduction: unreproduced: this is a claim about memory retention; the code structure answers it.
opus.evidence: Line 42: `const catalogues = new WeakMap<Factory["store"], { key: string; redact: HoldoutRedactor }>()`. Line 395 does `catalogues.set(store, ...)`, which overwrites the single entry for the daemon's one Store. Retention is therefore at most one catalogue, the one that was just built. It is the same allocation the request already needed, it is replaced on the next read for any run, and it never accumulates. The comment at lines 40-41 states this bound. There is no unbounded growth and no realistic memory failure.
opus.reason: The cache holds a single replaceable entry per store, so nothing grows without bound, though the later commit adds detail-count and character caps anyway.

title: A failed startup leaves started work running and drops the token's protection too early

codex.criterion: breaks a trust or confinement boundary
codex.failure_scenario: Startup resumes queued work and then fails, but does not reliably stop everything it started. Token-file protection can disappear before cleanup finishes, so sandbox policies constructed during that interval omit the credential’s read denial.
codex.evidence: At HEAD, `integrations = await mount(factory)` assigns no cleanup handle when mounting rejects. Real mounting calls `factory.land.start()` before awaiting tool versions (src/integrations/index.ts:47–58). The catch consequently evaluates `integrations?.stop()` as undefined and releases protection. Independently, startHttp calls `credential.release()` immediately on bind failure (src/server/http.ts:719–723), before startDaemon invokes integration cleanup. The partial-mount resource leak already exists at base, whose integration mounting has the same ordering; the premature removal of token protection is introduced by this change. The later commit registers component cleanups during mounting, cleans up before propagating rejection, and makes the daemon retain ownership of token protection until teardown settles.
codex.reason: The later commit addresses both partial-mount cleanup and premature token-protection release.

The new cleanup then cannot stop the half-mounted integrations, or it drops the token-file read-deny before the land queue has finished stopping. title: With enforcement on, a proxy-authenticated setup over plain HTTP can never authenticate

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator enables token enforcement for an accepted plain-HTTP proxy configuration. Browser sign-in cannot retain the required Secure cookie, leaving the operator repeatedly redirected to login and API requests unauthorized.
codex.evidence: HEAD retains `if (server.auth !== "proxy" && origins.some((o) => publicOrigin(o).startsWith("http:")))`, accepting HTTP origins in proxy mode even with enforcement enabled. The new authorization guard requires a bearer token or session regardless of proxy mode (src/server/http.ts:176–179). Auth.signIn emits a `__Host-limitless-session` cookie with `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` (src/server/auth.ts:14, 179–184), which ordinary non-loopback HTTP cannot support. Base has the same HTTPS exemption and Secure cookie, but proxy mode bypasses built-in session enforcement, so this configuration previously works. A bearer-equipped client can still authenticate; the failure concerns ordinary browser sign-in. The later commit rejects HTTP public origins under enforcement and updates OPERATIONS to explain the additional sign-in requirement.
codex.reason: The later commit rejects the unusable configuration with a clear error and corrects the proxy-authentication documentation.

title: A failed second bind releases token protection before the first listener has stopped

codex.criterion: breaks a trust or confinement boundary
codex.failure_scenario: If the second listener fails to start while the first listener’s shutdown is delayed, startup reports failure and removes the token-file protection while the first listener remains reachable. Agent sandbox profiles constructed during that interval omit the required token-file read denial.

codex.evidence: At HEAD, http.ts:735-738 executes `void local.stop(true); void lan?.stop(true); release(); throw error;`. In the daemon path, `server = startHttp(...)` never completes its assignment, so daemon.ts:19 awaits no listener and line 21 releases the credential after integration cleanup. The throwaway probe injected deferred shutdown around a real Bun listener and reproduced premature protection removal. This establishes the lifecycle/confinement defect, not an end-to-end authentication exploit: the second-bind failure occurs before the new token is published. Base also had `void local.stop(true)`, but had no token protection to release prematurely; that security-sensitive ordering is introduced by this change.
codex.reason: The later commit makes startHttp asynchronous, awaits both listener shutdowns before releasing protection and throwing, and makes startDaemon await startup before proceeding.

reproduction.output: after void stop: refused TypeError: ECONNREFUSED: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the u

opus.evidence: At head, src/server/http.ts:731-739 reads: `try { if (factory.cfg.listenLan) lan = bind(factory.cfg.listenLan); credential.publish(); } catch (error) { void local.stop(true); void lan?.stop(true); release(); throw error; }`. The stop calls are not awaited. For the daemon, release() in startHttp does nothing (the credential was supplied), and src/cli/daemon.ts's catch runs `await stop(true)`. That stop has `server` undefined because startHttp threw, so it calls `credential.release()` without the first listener's stop handle. This contrasts with the head's own normal stop(), which awaits both listeners before releasing. So the ordering defect is real. Its impact is small: (1) real Bun.serve closes the listening socket synchronously on stop(true), as reproduced, so the slow-stop window only exists with an injected serve; (2) every error reaching this catch happens before credential.publish() finishes, so this daemon's token is never on disk when the deny is lifted; (3) /api/health is meant to stay open, and factory.start() has not run, so no agents are running yet.
opus.reason: a98c3671 makes startHttp async, waits for both listeners' stop calls (Promise.allSettled) before release() in that catch, and startDaemon now awaits startHttp, which is exactly the claimed mechanism.

codex.failure_scenario: A reviewer reads a report that wraps a hidden verification observation across two lines. The hidden observation remains visible and can reach the implementer through review feedback, defeating the holdout boundary.

reproduction.output:

glows
Public checks passed."
BASE, same input: "Quoted result: the amber lantern
glows
Public checks passed."

codex.evidence: The temporary harness executes the exact buildCatalogue implementation copied from each revision, exposing the function through an added export and resolving its imports to installed dependencies; it supplies an in-memory database and synthetic verifier state. At head, line 326 selects only details already containing whitespace control characters: `const multilineDetails = [...details].filter((detail) => /[\r\n\t]/u.test(detail));`. Lines 347–355 then split report text into physical lines and test each independently. Consequently, neither fragment matches the single-line private evidence. Reports invoke this redactor through withoutHoldoutSection. Base also exposes this input, but the request explicitly requires report quotations of holdout material to remain withheld, making this a requirement gap.
codex.reason: The later commit matches all catalogue details across normalized whitespace; rerunning the harness against it withholds both quotation lines while preserving 'Public checks passed.'.

The change view hides that quote when it sits on one line but shows it in full when it is wrapped, so the owner's reviewer (and the next round's implementer, who reads the reviewer's findings) can see holdout result text that should stay hidden.

The holdoutRedact function (lines 339-358) then tests each line on its own: `value.split("\n").map((line) => { ... pattern.test(line) ... })`. The request requires that 'any report line that quotes it stays withheld', and the new tool description promises that verifier quotations are withheld. The input is uncommon: the factory's own renderReport puts table evidence through escapeCell, which collapses line breaks, and the holdout section is dropped whole. So a wrapped quote would mostly come from free-text sections such as the implementer summary or review text.
opus.reason: 5222fde builds the cross-line matcher from every catalogue detail with whitespace normalized (escaped forms included), and the repro then withholds both wrapped lines while 'Public checks passed.' stays visible.

title: The post-merge metadata read opens a window where a cancel is overwritten

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator cancels a landing while the factory fetches metadata after the merge. Cancellation reports success, but the subsequent completion overwrites the cancelled state with landed.

reproduction.output:
F1 before cancel=merging
F1 cancel returned=true, state=cancelled, aborted=true
F1 after metadata abort=landed

codex.evidence: The temporary probe used the real HEAD queue and in-memory Store, mocked mergePullRequest to return 'merged', and injected a metadata client that rejects on cancellation. HEAD awaits the client with '.catch(() => null)' at line 620, then unconditionally calls landed(). cancel() records 'cancelled', while finish() unconditionally updates the entry state. Base called 'this.landed(entry, run, sha)' immediately after the successful merge, without this additional await. The defect concerns cancellation state; the merge has already happened.
codex.reason: The later commit records landing before fetching metadata, guards terminal entries, and bounds metadata enrichment to 30 seconds without changing land state.

opus.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: An operator cancels a land just after GitHub has merged the PR, while the queue is still fetching who merged it and when. The cancel reports success and the entry shows 'cancelled', then a moment later it flips to 'landed'. The final record is accurate because the PR did merge, but the operator was told their cancel worked when it did not.

reproduction.command: copy of test/land-queue.test.ts under $TMPDIR with absolute imports, plus a test whose client blocks the post-merge read until it is aborted; then q.cancel(entry.id); bun test $TMPDIR/adj520/repro.test.ts -t REPRO
reproduction.output:
state before cancel: merging
cancel returned: true
state right after cancel: cancelled
final state: landed merged b335a017c454
feed kinds: [ "land.queued", "land.landed" ]

opus.evidence: Head queue.ts:620-621: `const observed = await (this.deps.client ?? getGitHubPr)(entry.prUrl, signal).catch(() => null); this.landed(...)`. landed() then calls `this.finish(entry.id, "landed", ...)` without checking the current state. At base, `this.landed(entry, run, sha)` ran right after mergePullRequest with nothing awaited in between. cancel() (lines 254-259) aborts and finishes the entry as 'cancelled', and the swallowed abort lets landed() overwrite it. The persisted outcome ('landed') matches reality, so the cost is a wrong cancel reply and a brief state flip, not lost work.
opus.reason: The later commit records the landing in a state-checked transaction before an abort-bounded metadata read, so a cancel after the merge returns false and the metadata read only fills run fields.

title: Marking the owner merged can resolve the landed round as superseded

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator lands a review round awaiting human attention whose original request closes the same issue as its parent. The factory permanently records that round as superseded instead of resolved by its merge.

reproduction.output:
F2 after landed={"status":"resolved","merged":true,"resolution":"superseded"}
F2 after reconciliation={"status":"resolved","merged":true,"resolution":"superseded"}

codex.evidence: The temporary probe created a succeeded owner and needs_human review round with the real Store, generated the round prompt with reviewRoundPrompt(), and invoked HEAD landed() with a MERGED observation. HEAD loops over '[run.id, owner.id]' and calls updateRun() with 'merged: true'. Store.updateRun() calls supersedeByIssue(), whose exclusion is only 'r.id !== merged.id'; consequently the owner update supersedes the still-needs_human round. Calling resolveMergedRun() afterward preserved that resolution. Base landed() updated only the entry's run: 'this.store.updateRun(run.id, { merged: true })', so this owner-triggered supersession was absent.
codex.reason: The later commit resolves both landing runs through resolveMergedRun() and excludes their IDs from supersession, including when merge metadata is missing.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: A review round that is waiting on a human gets approved and landed. Its prompt repeats the original request's 'Closes #N'. When the queue marks the parent run merged, the round that just landed is closed as 'superseded' by its own PR instead of 'merged'. Later reconciliation skips it, so the wrong resolution stays permanently.

reproduction.command: same scratch copy: a needs_human round and its owner both saying 'Closes #42'; land the round; print the resolutions. Run against head, and against a git-archive copy of base

HEAD: round: {"merged":true,"status":"resolved","resolution":{"kind":"superseded","ref":"https://github.com/test/repo/pull/1",...}} owner: {"merged":true,"status":"succeeded"}
BASE: round: {"merged":true,"status":"needs_human","resolution":null} owner: {"merged":false,...} (reconciliation's resolveMergedRun later resolves it as merged)

opus.evidence: Head landed() loops over `new Set([run.id, owner.id])` and calls `this.store.updateRun(id, { merged: true, ... })`. updateRun runs `if (patch.merged) this.supersedeByIssue(run)`, which excludes only the run being updated. reviewRoundPrompt embeds `## Original request\n${request}`, so the round's prompt keeps the 'Closes #N'. Base only updated the entry's run. At head, reconcileMergedRuns skips runs where `run.merged && run.status !== "needs_human"` and only fills metadata, so the superseded resolution is never corrected.
opus.reason: The later commit routes each landed run through resolveMergedRun with excludeFromSupersession set to the landed ids, and adds a test that the needs_human round resolves as merged.

title: Landing publishes before its outer transaction commits, and never drains the feed

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An agent watching a landing can receive a merge notification before the database commits, even if the landing subsequently rolls back. Successful landing feed items can also remain unpublished until another operation publishes something.
codex.evidence: The temporary probe invoked the actual landing method with an isolated store, subscribed to publications, and injected failure in the second merge resolver. HEAD wraps landing in `this.store.db.transaction(...)`, while store.ts:668-681 independently buffers and publishes each nested chatTransaction after its savepoint returns. Its publishFeed returns when `this.db.inTransaction` is true (line 686). Landing performs no drain after the outer commit. Base had no outer landing transaction; the equivalent successful probe delivered both feed items with inTransaction=false.
codex.reason: The later commit uses the publication-buffered Store.transaction for the whole landing; the same probes then delivered publications after commit, drained the feed immediately, and emitted nothing on rollback.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: When the land queue records a merge, the 'landed' and 'merged' feed items are written but never pushed to live feed listeners such as the UI stream or an agent long-polling the feed. Those listeners stay asleep until some unrelated event happens. The run update is also sent to listeners before the landing transaction has committed, so if that transaction rolled back they would already have seen a change that never happened.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/f1repro/f1.test.ts  (a throwaway test that runs updateLandEntry + landFeed + resolveMergedRun inside a raw store.db.transaction, exactly as LandQueue.landed() does, with a subscriber logging each message and db.inTransaction)
reproduction.output:
after commit: ["run inTx=true"]
feed rows: run.pr_opened,run.succeeded,land.landed,run.merged
after unrelated publish: ["run inTx=true","feed:land.landed inTx=false","feed:run.merged inTx=false","run inTx=false"]

opus.evidence: At head, landed() does `this.store.db.transaction(() => { ... this.finish(...); for (const id of ids) this.store.resolveMergedRun(...) })()`. That raw transaction leaves pendingPublications null. updateRun/resolveRun then call chatTransaction, which publishes its buffered messages as soon as its inner savepoint returns, while the outer transaction is still open. publishFeed() starts with `if (this.db.inTransaction || this.feedPublishing) return;`, so neither chatTransaction's drain nor landFeed's drain runs, and nothing drains after the outer commit. At base, landed() called updateRun (its own top-level chatTransaction) and then finish → landFeed → publishFeed outside any transaction, so the feed was drained. The merge path drains later only if the optional metadata read returns MERGED (through fillMergedRunMetadata's chatTransaction). A PR found already merged in awaitCi, or a failed metadata read, is never drained.
opus.reason: The later commit makes chatTransaction a public store.transaction, which buffers publications and drains the feed after the outermost commit, and landed() now runs through it.

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator cancels a landing while its pull-request lookup is pending, and the lookup subsequently confirms that the pull request merged. The entry remains cancelled, but the runs retain stale merge information until a separate reconciliation discovers the merge.

Landing's `if (!this.isActive(this.store.getLandEntry(entry.id) ?? entry)) return;` precedes every resolveMergedRun call. Startup processes only active entries. Base recorded the merge unconditionally, although it incorrectly overwrote the cancelled entry as landed.
codex.reason: The later commit guards only the entry transition and always records the confirmed PR merge; the same probe then preserved cancellation while marking both runs merged.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/f1repro/f23.test.ts  (F2 case: awaitCi with polling off and a client that resolves MERGED after the signal is aborted and the entry set to cancelled, then landed() is called with that observation)

opus.evidence: At head: `this.store.db.transaction(() => { if (!this.isActive(this.store.getLandEntry(entry.id) ?? entry)) return; this.finish(...); for (const id of ids) this.store.resolveMergedRun(...) })()`. The early return skips the run merge records as well as the entry transition. awaitCi returns `seen` after `await this.observe(...)` without checking the signal again, so a MERGED observation can arrive after cancel. Base's landed() called `updateRun(run.id, { merged: true })` unconditionally, so the merge was recorded (base also overwrote cancelled with landed). Cancelled entries are not resumed (start() lists only active entries). The log line still says 'merged' even though nothing was recorded.
opus.reason: The later commit runs finish only when the entry is active, but always calls resolveMergedPr for the PR's runs.

title: Landing through the owner run still supersedes the PR's own rounds

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator lands a pull request through its original run while a review round for the same issue awaits attention. The review round is recorded as superseded instead of merged, and subsequent merge reconciliation preserves that incorrect resolution.
codex.evidence: For an owner-run entry, `const owner = this.store.reviewRound(run.id)?.owner ?? run; const ids = [...new Set([run.id, owner.id])];` contains only the owner. updateRun then invokes supersedeByIssue, whose exclusion check at store.ts:1892-1894 does not protect its rounds. codex.reason: The later commit shares resolveMergedPr between landing and reconciliation, resolving all runs for that PR while excluding them from supersession; the same probe then recorded the round's resolution as merged.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
