codex.failure_scenario: A worker session reports a local path using a temporary-directory alias or escaped slashes. The worker sends that private filesystem path, potentially including a username, to the coordinator in events and results.

reproduction.output: {"probe":"mask","scratchPrefix":"/private/var/","eventMasked":{"literalCheckout":true,"literalScratch":true,"aliasScratch":false,"escapedCheckout":false,"escapedScratch":false},"resultMasked":{"literalCheckout":true,"literalScratch":true,"aliasScratch":false,"escapedCheckout":false,"escapedScratch":false}}

codex.evidence: The temporary probe exercised HEAD's real worker loop with fake transport and harnesses; Git operations and the shared runner were mocked, with canonical scratch supplied to the harness. HEAD masks serialized data using `text.replaceAll(JSON.stringify(path).slice(1, -1), "<worktree>")`. Its `spellings(...)` includes supplied and canonical paths, but does not generate inverse temporary-directory aliases from canonical paths or escaped-slash variants. Both event batches and results use this sanitizer, and both leaked the tested variants. Base had no worker agent execution or reporting path. The later commit adds `agentPathMask`, explicitly expands /tmp and /var aliases in both directions, captures canonical spellings, and matches escaped slashes longest first. Running the same probe against temporary copies of the later modules reported true for every masking case.
codex.reason: The newly introduced sanitizer misses alternate path representations, and the later commit addresses that mechanism in event and result reporting.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: The worker hands the agent its scratch directory as /private/tmp/lr-XXXX/claude-501. If the session (or a tool it runs) prints that same directory as /tmp/lr-XXXX/claude-501, or prints the checkout path with escaped slashes (\/Users\/name\/...), the real path goes to the coordinator unmasked. With the escaped form, that includes the worker owner's username.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/s.ts  (createScratch + spellings, then the same JSON-replace reduce that runAgent's sanitize uses)
reproduction.output:
scratch /private/tmp/lr-qDE1QX/claude-501 spellings [ "/private/tmp/lr-qDE1QX/claude-501" ]
{"text":"wrote /tmp/lr-qDE1QX/claude-501/out.txt and \\/Users\\/<user>\\/.adjtest-OYkWqA"}

opus.evidence: client.ts:461-467 `sanitize` replaces only `JSON.stringify(path).slice(1,-1)` for each entry of `spellings([...])`. policySpellings returns only `resolve(path)` and its realpath. createScratch already realpaths its base (`/private/tmp`), so the list has a single entry and the `/tmp` alias is never added. Escaped-slash forms are never matched either. Both alias forms need session output that spells the path differently from how it was given, which the request ("replace the worker's checkout and scratch paths") doesn't explicitly ask to handle. The /tmp case leaks only a random temp directory with a uid. The username leak needs a tool that escapes slashes.
opus.reason: The later commit's agentPathMask adds /tmp↔/private/tmp and /var↔/private/var aliases, keeps the original and realpath spellings, and matches escaped slashes with a regex, longest pattern first.

title: Fencing fires up to one heartbeat interval after the lease has expired

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: A worker loses contact with the coordinator after a delayed successful heartbeat. Its agent keeps spending quota beyond the required lease deadline until the next periodic fence check.

reproduction.output: {"probe":"fence","leaseMs":400,"heartbeatMs":200,"secondHeartbeatDelayMs":100,"abortAfterLastSuccessMs":501}

codex.evidence: The temporary probe exercised HEAD's real worker loop and timers with fake transport and a harness waiting for cancellation; checkout operations were mocked and no network was used. The second heartbeat succeeded after an injected 100 ms delay, and subsequent heartbeats failed. HEAD records `lastHeartbeat = performance.now()` but checks `performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs` only inside `setInterval(..., Math.min(options.heartbeatMs ?? timing.heartbeat, leaseMs))`. Successful heartbeats do not realign that interval, leaving a systematic window beyond the deadline; cancellation occurred after 501 ms for a 400 ms lease. Base had no agent-job fence. The later commit clears and schedules a lease-duration timeout after each successful heartbeat and clears it during shutdown. The same probe against temporary copies of the later modules measured 401 ms.
codex.reason: Periodic sampling permits agent execution beyond the promised fencing deadline, and the later commit replaces it with a timeout scheduled from each successful heartbeat.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: A worker loses contact with the coordinator. The coordinator expires the lease after one lease period (60 s by default), but the worker only checks every heartbeat interval (10 s), so its agent session can keep spending model quota for up to about 10 s more. In that window the job may already be re-leased to another worker.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: timing-dependent; no throwaway timing harness was run here. The bound follows directly from the quoted interval code.
opus.evidence: client.ts:552-558: `fence = setInterval(() => { if (performance.now() - lastHeartbeat > leaseMs) for (const job of agentJobs.values()) job.controller.abort(); }, Math.min(options.heartbeatMs ?? timing.heartbeat, leaseMs));`. lastHeartbeat is set only when a reply arrives (line 314). The abort therefore lands somewhere between leaseMs and leaseMs+heartbeatMs after the last success. protocol.ts sets heartbeat 10_000 and lease 60_000. The requirement is met only to within one heartbeat interval. The cost is a bounded, short overrun during a partition.
opus.reason: The later commit replaces the polling interval with a one-shot timer that is re-armed for leaseMs on every successful heartbeat and cleared on shutdown.

title: Restart deletes retained directories when no process identity was recorded

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: An agent starts a detached descendant, and process discovery fails before recording any identity. Restarting the worker deletes the retained checkout, scratch and cleanup metadata while that descendant remains alive, allowing it to keep running alongside retried work.
codex.evidence: The throwaway test exercised real worker execution, retention and restart with a real detached descendant; Git operations and coordinator requests were mocked, with no network or Git writes. At HEAD, src/util/proc.ts:535-557 discovers processes before calling recordProcessCleanup, so first-scan failure leaves zero identities. Recovery immediately returns on `if (!records.length) return;` (line 115). Worker startup then calls `await cleanup(job)` and subsequently `delete retained[id]; save();` without positive termination confirmation. Its fresh scope has no previous termination error. Base already deleted directories after failed jobs and lacked worker retention/recovery, so HEAD incompletely satisfies the explicit retention requirement. The later commit persists discovery context immediately after spawn, recovers invocations without identity rows, and refuses startup cleanup when evidence or confirmation is missing.
codex.reason: HEAD treats absent process identities as permission to delete retained directories; the later commit requires durable discovery evidence and confirmed termination.

opus.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
opus.failure_scenario: A worker job's process cleanup fails before any process has been recorded, for example because the first process scan or the macOS process-leader capture fails. The worker correctly keeps the job's checkout and scratch, but on its next start it finds nothing to confirm and deletes those directories while a descendant of the job may still be running. That descendant can then overlap a retried job and keep spending quota.

reproduction.command: Copied test/workers.test.ts to $TMPDIR/f1.ApTZ/f1.test.ts with imports rewritten to absolute paths. In the test 'worker retains a %s job after discovery failure...' I made one change: the injected scanner now fails on the first environment scan (`++scans > 1` became `++scans > 0`). The assertions after `worker.stop()` were replaced by prints, followed by one plain `runWorker` restart that aborts on its first coordinator request. Ran: bun test $TMPDIR/f1.ApTZ/f1.test.ts -t 'job after discovery failure'
reproduction.output:
F1 after failure: records [] root exists true scratch exists true
F1 after restart: root exists false checkout exists false scratch exists false descendant alive true
(identical for both the agent and gate parameterizations; 2 pass)

opus.evidence: At head, src/workers/client.ts:436-441 (`finish`) handles a termination error only by saving the directories: `retained[root] = { root, cache, scratch: [...scope.scratchDirs] }; save(); throw ...`. It writes no row to process_cleanups. Rows are written only through `recordProcessCleanup`, which `stopMarkedProcesses` calls after a successful scan. There are two ways to end up with zero rows: a first-scan failure, and the leader-capture error that src/util/proc.ts:841 throws before any scan (`if (leaderInspectionError) throw leaderInspectionError;`). At startup, client.ts:280 calls `await recoverProcessCleanups(store);`, which returns at once when `!records.length`. The loop at client.ts:281-300 (`for (const [id, job] of Object.entries(retained))`) then calls `cleanup(job)`. That runs `git worktree remove` and `removeScratch` on the scratch directories and the root without ever confirming that the old invocation's processes are gone, and then drops the retained entry. The cleanup's own git process scans only its own new marker, so it never finds the old job's descendants. The issue requires keeping the checkout and scratch until termination is confirmed, and this path deletes them without confirmation.
opus.reason: Commit 8ba8533 fixes this in three parts. `startProcess` now records discovery context through `recordProcessDiscovery` right after spawn, before any shutdown scan. Startup now throws 'missing worker discovery evidence' for a retained job that has no discoveries. It also refuses any retained job that isn't `confirmed` ('unresolved worker cleanup'), so neither the first-scan failure nor the leader-capture failure can lead to unconfirmed deletion.

title: Record a kept job as unconfirmed before its first process starts, and confirm it only from positive evidence

codex.criterion: stops the factory or the running release from working
codex.failure_scenario: A worker crashes just after launching another command, and its next start deletes the job’s directories while that command remains alive. Alternatively, a temporary inspection failure leaves incomplete cleanup evidence that prevents the worker from starting again, even after a reboot.

reproduction.output: Seeded stale confirmed record with an owned live child: rootExists=false, scratchExists=false, childAlive=true, scans=0, requests=0; startup subsequently stopped at the intentionally absent token file. Seeded unconfirmed record with empty discoveries: both startup attempts threw "Invocation termination could not be confirmed: missing worker discovery evidence", retained both directories, and performed zero scans or requests; the second attempt supplied a different boot identity.

codex.evidence: The temporary, network-free probe exercised HEAD’s actual Store and runWorker against seeded recovery snapshots; it did not reproduce an actual worker crash. The crash window follows directly from HEAD: proc.ts:801 calls "const child = spawn(bin, args, {", but discovery persistence occurs at lines 822–828 and evaluates "boot: bootIdentity()" first. client.ts:247 previously persists "job.confirmed = job.discoveries.length === 0", so a completed command can leave confirmation that survives the next spawn. Startup skips such entries at line 318 and removes their directories at lines 333–350 without discovering the unrecorded child. If bootIdentity throws, no discovery callback executes; proc.ts:867 rejects termination confirmation, and client.ts:489–497 retains the job with confirmed:false. Startup then throws at lines 323–326 when no discovery evidence exists, before heartbeat processing; changing boot identity cannot help because recovery is never reached. Base had neither this worker cleanup ledger nor these startup rejection paths, although orphaned processes on worker crashes were already the issue being addressed.
codex.reason: The later commit persists job ownership before spawning, adds an inherited job marker and before-spawn persistence, confirms cleanup through scanning or a changed boot identity, and logs unresolved entries while retrying on heartbeats instead of refusing startup.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: If a worker job's process cleanup can't be confirmed before any discovery record was saved (boot-identity inspection fails, or a harness raises the termination error itself), the worker refuses to start on every later attempt until someone edits its database by hand. Separately, if the worker is killed just after it starts a new child, an earlier command's "confirmed" mark lets the next start delete the checkout while that child may still be running and spending quota.

reproduction.output:
attempt 0 Error: Invocation termination could not be confirmed: missing worker discovery evidence requests 0 checkout kept true
attempt 1 ... missing worker discovery evidence requests 0 checkout kept true
attempt 2 ... missing worker discovery evidence requests 0 checkout kept true

opus.evidence: (b) At head, src/workers/client.ts startup: `if (job.confirmed || job.discoveries?.length) continue; job.discoveries = store.listProcessCleanups(undefined, join(job.root, "checkout"))...; if (!job.discoveries.length) throw new ProcessTerminationError(`...: missing worker discovery evidence`)`. This throw happens inside runWorker's main try, before any request is made, so the worker exits. Nothing in the code ever moves such an entry forward. In src/util/proc.ts:822-831 the record is built with `boot: bootIdentity()` inside the argument list, so a throw there skips recordProcessDiscovery and only sets discoveryError. Then `finish` saves `{...retained[root], confirmed:false}` with no discoveries. Head's own test at test/workers.test.ts:5016 confirms this state is reachable (`discoveries: [], confirmed: false`), and the legacy test at :2589 asserts the permanent refusal. (a) `deleteInvocationCleanups` sets `job.confirmed = job.discoveries.length === 0`, so after a successful command the entry is saved with confirmed:true. The next `spawn` (proc.ts:813) comes before `recordProcessDiscovery` (proc.ts:822). If the worker is killed in that window, the next start skips the entry as confirmed, and `cleanup(job)` removes the checkout without scanning for the detached child. I did not reproduce (a): the window is synchronous (leader capture plus one SQLite write), so a reproduction needs a SIGKILL timed inside it. The mechanism is clear from the code.

It confirms an entry from a marker scan or a changed boot identity. Startup and later attempts now log unresolved entries (`unresolved(error)`) instead of refusing to start, which addresses both (a) and (b).

title: An empty scan without the invocation's discovery record must not confirm a kept job; wait for a changed boot instead

codex.criterion: loses or corrupts persisted state
codex.failure_scenario: A worker dies after launching a job process but before saving its discovery information. On restart, an empty scan incorrectly confirms termination, deletes the job’s directories and durable cleanup entry, and leaves the process running without recovery records.

reproduction.output: Both throwaway runs seeded a retained job without discovery records, launched a marked shell that changed outside the job roots and executed sleep, and exited its launcher. Native macOS scanning returned: {"mode":"native-macos-scan","processAlive":true,"rootExists":false,"scratchExists":false,"retainedJobs":0,"cleanupRecords":0,"diagnostics":[]}. Injected empty scanning returned the same results. Boot identity was injected as an unchanged value because the sandbox denied the native boot query; coordinator requests and confinement were injected, with no network access.

codex.evidence: At HEAD, client.ts:356-361 saves scratch and 'job.confirmed = false' before spawning, but saves no invocation marker. proc.ts:818-819 calls 'scope?.beforeSpawn?.()' then spawns; discovery persistence occurs afterward at 842-849. Without that record, client.ts:284-303 supplies fallback discovery with 'group: 0', 'leader: null', and 'spawnedAt: "0"'. Two empty scans satisfy proc.ts:235-237 and return successfully; client.ts:373-391 then removes directories and executes 'delete retained[id]; save()'. A platform process with hidden environment outside the roots cannot be identified by that fallback. Base had no worker cleanup store or this recovery-confirmation path. The later commit persists a pending-marker set before spawn, clears markers after saved discovery or confirmed live termination, and refuses recovery without discovery evidence until a changed boot is established, recording the first readable boot when necessary.
codex.reason: The later commit addresses the missing pre-spawn evidence and prevents empty scans from retiring cleanup obligations for invocations whose discovery context was never saved.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: A worker keeps a failed job's folders because it couldn't confirm the job's processes had stopped. But it never saved the discovery record for one of the processes it started, either because it crashed right after starting it or because saving the record failed. After a restart, recovery runs a weaker fallback scan that can't see a system binary that has moved its working directory outside the job folders. That scan finds nothing, so recovery deletes the checkout and scratch while the process may still be running and overlapping a retried job.

reproduction.command: Ported the later commit's test 'pending recovery requires a changed boot while saved null-leader context and new jobs recover independently' to $TMPDIR/f1repro/f1.test.ts, with imports rewritten to point at the head sources, then ran: bun test --preload <repo>/test/setup.ts ./f1.test.ts -t 'pending recovery requires a changed boot'. The test pre-seeds a kept entry that has an ownership marker and no discovery record for the pending invocation (head ignores the extra 'pending' field), injects discover() => [], and restarts runWorker with the same boot identity.
reproduction.output: On the first same-boot restart: expect(existsSync(root)).toBe(true) gives Expected: true, Received: false. The job root was removed after an empty fallback scan. (fail) pending recovery requires a changed boot ... 0 pass, 1 fail

opus.evidence: At head, src/workers/client.ts:280-300 confirm() scans an entry that has ownership with a made-up context when it has no saved discovery for that invocation: `discovery: { group: 0, started: owner.started, directories: [job.root, ...job.scratch]..., leader: null, spawnedAt: "0" }`. In recoverProcessCleanups (src/util/proc.ts:235), two empty scans with that context count as confirmation and the records are deleted. recover() (client.ts:359-385) then calls cleanup(job), which removes the root and scratch. With group 0 and no leader, markedDarwinProcesses can't add anything by session or group membership. hiddenDarwinProcessMember (processes-darwin.ts:104-135) only claims a hidden-environment process that descends from a member, or an orphan whose working directory is inside the job folders. So a system binary that has left those folders is invisible, and processes-darwin.ts:107-108 itself names this residual. A saved discovery record would carry the leader's session and group, which proves membership. The discovery record is only missing if the process crashes in the synchronous window between spawn and recordProcessDiscovery (proc.ts:818-851), or if saving the record fails, in which case head kills the direct child at once (`if (discoveryError) void terminate()`). That narrow trigger is why I rated this minor. `confirmed` is only ever assigned false (client.ts:356, and in the entry built for a new job) and never read.
opus.reason: 65c67010 records each invocation marker as pending before spawn through beforeSpawn(marker) and clears it when the discovery record is saved or termination is confirmed. confirm() now refuses to treat a pending marker that has no saved discovery as confirmed until the boot identity changes, recording the current boot when none was saved. The unused `confirmed` field is replaced by the pending list, and the ported test of that behaviour fails at head.

title: Check everything the push publishes: the full range from the remote head or base, and the branch name

codex.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a branch containing an earlier unpublished commit with private information, or a branch whose name contains private information. The publication checks pass and the private information reaches the remote.

The coordinator already checks branch text and uses deliveryPublicationRange. Base had no worker publication implementation. A session therefore cannot perform the commit required by the claim without a separate confinement breach. Actual Seatbelt enforcement was unreproduced here because nested sandbox application was denied.

codex.failure_scenario: A developer starts the source daemon with the packaging flag set by caller Bun settings or a runtime global. Startup fails with a misleading missing-embedded-UI error, although this installation should build its UI from source.

reproduction.command: Run temporary probe.ts files from separate directories, importing HEAD's release.ts and ui.ts and calling buildUi(): baseline; globalThis.LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED=true before import; caller bunfig.toml containing [define] LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED="true".
reproduction.output:
Bun 1.4.3:
baseline: release.kind=source; buildUi=success (3 assets)
runtime-global: release.kind=source; buildUi=Packaged Limitless is missing its embedded UI or index.html
caller-bunfig: release.kind=source; buildUi=Packaged Limitless is missing its embedded UI or index.html

codex.evidence: HEAD requires both `(typeof LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED === "undefined" || !LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED)` and `info.kind === "source"` before compiling. A foreign true value therefore sends a source release into the embedded-file loader. Base's buildUi unconditionally builds from source and never reads this symbol. The consequence requires an unusual override of an internal build symbol; the claim explicitly accepts a clear refusal instead of successful startup, so this is minor rather than a general factory outage.
codex.reason: The later commit checks info.kind first and explicitly refuses a foreign true define with a message naming the symbol and both possible origins, while retaining the compile-time import guard.

kind source
ERR Packaged Limitless is missing its embedded UI or index.html: ~/…/limitless-781-r2/limitless-ui
(bunfig variant) ERR Packaged Limitless is missing its embedded UI or index.html: ~/…/limitless-781-r2/limitless-ui

title: Cover staging cleanup and the packaged map's source

codex.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
codex.failure_scenario: A future change leaves stale staging files behind or rebuilds the packaged UI from source. The existing tests can stay green, failing to detect those packaging regressions.

reproduction.command: In a temporary copy under $TMPDIR, run `bun test test/ui-build.test.ts --timeout 30000` on HEAD, then independently remove staging cleanup and change the source-build condition to also compile packaged releases whose embedded index exists.
reproduction.output:
HEAD baseline: 5 pass, 0 fail
Staging cleanup removed: 5 pass, 0 fail
Packaged loader recompiles from source: 5 pass, 0 fail
Separate HEAD behavior probe: staging contains exactly build outputs=true; packaged Bun.build calls=0; all packaged blobs reference embedded directory=true.

codex.evidence: The HEAD fixture stages into a fresh temporary directory without seeding stale entries. Its equality test only compares filenames, bytes and content types, which recompilation reproduces; neither the fixture nor that test checks builder calls or embedded-file provenance. The authorization test consumes these same maps and therefore cannot distinguish their origin. HEAD's production behavior is correct: stageUi removes the directory, and the packaged loader calls Bun.file for each embedded entry. This is solely a coverage gap against the explicit mutation-sensitivity requirement. Only the five UI build tests were executed; the claimed 27-test total was not independently verified.
codex.reason: The later commit seeds stale files and nested directories, checks staging against build outputs, forbids packaged builder calls, and verifies embedded-file provenance using an independently altered asset.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle, or the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: A later change could stop the release build from clearing old UI files before staging, or make the packaged daemon recompile the UI instead of reading the embedded files. The current tests would still pass, so stale or wrongly sourced UI files could ship unnoticed.

No stale files are seeded, and no spy on Bun.build exists. test/ui-build.test.ts:33-42 only checks that keys, types and bytes match the source build. scripts/build-binary.ts stageUi does `rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true })`, and no test exercises that line.

title: An interrupt during the drain request can leave the daemon draining

codex.criterion: stops the factory or the running release from working
codex.failure_scenario: An operator interrupts a restart while its drain request is still pending. Cleanup resumes scheduling first, but the delayed drain then pauses it indefinitely, preventing new runs until someone manually resumes it.

reproduction.output:
{"operation":"restart","events":["drain sent","SIGINT","resume applied","command rejected","drain applied"],"exitedBeforeDrain":true,"lockReleasedBeforeDrain":true,"finalDraining":true,"kickstarts":0,"error":"Error: restart interrupted by SIGINT"}
{"operation":"deploy","events":["drain sent","SIGINT","resume applied","command rejected","drain applied"],"exitedBeforeDrain":true,"lockReleasedBeforeDrain":true,"finalDraining":true,"kickstarts":0,"error":"Error: deploy failed; rollback attempted to previous\nError: deploy interrupted by SIGINT"}

codex.evidence: At HEAD, line 536 executes `await race(requestAdmin(client, clock, "drain"))`; SIGINT rejects that race without settling the independently bounded admin request. Before kickstart, the catch path immediately executes `await requestAdmin(client, clock, "resume")` at line 554. The throwaway probe injected a deferred drain, emitted SIGINT, observed cleanup and lock release, then applied the drain; both restart and deploy ended draining with zero kickstarts. Base already has this race in deploy (lines 622 and 658), but HEAD introduces it into the new restart command, violating its interrupt recovery requirement. The existing restart test applies drain before emitting SIGINT, so it misses this ordering.
codex.reason: The later commit adds a shared requestDrain helper that waits for the bounded drain promise to settle before propagating interruption, uses it in restart, deploy and install, and adds deferred-drain regression coverage.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: An operator presses Ctrl-C during the few milliseconds while the restart's drain request is still in flight. The restart sends a resume, gets an acknowledgement and exits, and then the late drain takes effect. The daemon stays drained and starts no new runs until someone resumes it by hand.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/f1probe/probe.test.ts  (throwaway test: injected fake client whose drain call emits SIGINT and only applies draining=true after restart() has returned; fake command/clock as in test/restart.test.ts)
reproduction.output:
log daemon before: release
send drain
log interrupted, stopping restart...
send resume
daemon applied resume
restart returned: Error: restart interrupted by SIGINT
daemon applied drain
final draining: true

opus.evidence: At head, src/cli/service.ts:536 has `if (!running.draining) await race(requestAdmin(client, clock, "drain"));`. Here `race` is `Promise.race([work, signal])` (serviceControl), so a SIGINT rejects at once while the drain request keeps running: `requestAdmin` and `bounded` use their own AbortController, and nothing aborts it on interrupt. The catch at lines 544-556 then sends `requestAdmin(client, clock, "resume")` without waiting for the pending drain to settle. The daemon handles drain and resume synchronously (http.ts:280-284), so whichever arrives last wins. Deploy at base already had the same `race(requestAdmin(..., "drain"))` pattern, and install has it at line 368. The restart function itself is new, so this restart path is introduced code that copies a preexisting flaw. In production, two localhost requests seldom arrive out of order, which is why this is rated minor despite the silent consequence.
opus.reason: The later commit adds a shared requestDrain helper that, after an interrupt, awaits the pending drain request (still bounded by its request timeout) before rethrowing, and uses it in restart, deploy and install; this removes the ordering race the probe shows.

title: A live owner's held slot expires during an event-loop stall, so two holders run at limit 1

codex.failure_scenario: When an owner misses renewal long enough, another instance admits waiting work while the original work can continue. This reproduces the expiry behavior explicitly required by the request.

reproduction.output: F1 {"time":31000,"activeA":true,"activeB":true,"snapshot":{"occupied":1,"limit":1,"holders":["B"]}}

codex.evidence: The temporary probe withheld A's timer callbacks while advancing the injected clock and running B's callback. HEAD deletes rows using `(renewed_at <= ? OR lease_until <= ?)`. However, the request expressly requires that an instance which stops renewing 'loses its held slot after the expiry period, and a waiter elsewhere gets it.' Its ownership rule does not distinguish a stalled process from a dead one. 'Held slots are never interrupted' describes non-preemption; neither process's work is interrupted here. Base's ordinary acquisitions did not expire, but introducing expiry was explicitly requested. HEAD's targeted expiry test also passed: 1 pass, 0 fail.
codex.reason: The later commit replaces timestamp expiry for ordinary reservations with PID and process-birth inspection, addressing the demonstrated mechanism by changing the requested ownership policy.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: If the daemon's event loop freezes for about 20 seconds or more while it holds a gate slot, another process's next poll deletes that held slot and starts its own suite. Two full suites then run at limit 1, and the first process is never told it lost the slot.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/adj/claims.test.ts (pool A acquires, then its timers never fire to simulate a stalled loop; pool B queues; the shared clock advances 31 s in 250 ms steps)
reproduction.output: F1 B admitted while A never released: true { occupied: 1, limit: 1, holders: [ "B" ] }

opus.evidence: At head, refresh() deletes held in-process rows by timestamp: `DELETE FROM slot_requests WHERE pool = ? AND (renewed_at <= ? OR lease_until <= ?)` with `this.now() - GATE_LEASE_EXPIRY_MS`. renewed_at is only bumped by the owner's own pulse, at the 10 s renewal interval. Nothing tells the holder its acquire() was revoked. Base never expired in-process holders. The issue does ask that rows of an owner that stops renewing expire after GATE_LEASE_EXPIRY_MS, so this only goes wrong when a live owner stalls for more than about 20 s, which is an unusual condition.
opus.reason: The later commit drops timestamp expiry for in-process rows and deletes them only when the recorded pid has a different process birth time (owner_pid/owner_birth plus inspect), so a stalled but live owner keeps its slot.

title: A waiting external lease loses its queue position across a daemon restart

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: A client waiting for capacity contacts the restarted daemon and is told its reservation expired. Its abandoned reservation can then occupy the available slot while its replacement remains waiting, delaying work and losing its queue position.

reproduction.output: F2 {"heartbeat":"undefined","release":"undefined","replacementAcquired":false,"snapshot":{"occupied":1,"limit":1,"holders":["original-client"]},"rows":[{"holder":"original-client","state":"held"},{"holder":"replacement-client","state":"waiting"}]}

codex.evidence: The probe closed the original pool after creating a waiting lease, constructed a replacement owner, attempted heartbeat and release, re-requested, then freed the blocker. HEAD rejects both operations through `(row.owner !== this.owner && row.state !== "held")`. The HTTP endpoint translates undefined into `expired: true`, and the ordinary CLI clears its lease ID and re-requests. The surviving original row is nevertheless eligible for admission. Base also forgot waiting clients on restart, but its in-memory queue disappeared; it could not leave this persisted phantom holder.
codex.reason: The later commit removes the waiting-row ownership restriction, preserves queue ordering during adoption, permits cross-owner external release, and prevents stale callbacks from deleting adopted leases.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: A `gate-slot` client is waiting in the queue when the daemon restarts. After the restart its heartbeat and its release both come back as expired, so it has to queue again at the back, and its abandoned old request can still be granted a slot and block capacity for up to 30 seconds.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/adj/claims.test.ts (old pool holds the slot and creates a waiting lease, then closes; a new-owner pool heartbeats and releases the lease id)
reproduction.output:
F2 before restart heartbeat: false
F2 after restart heartbeat: undefined release: undefined { occupied: 1, limit: 1, holders: [ "held" ] }

opus.evidence: heartbeat(): `if (!row || row.lease_until === null || (row.owner !== this.owner && row.state !== "held")) return;` refuses a waiting row owned by the previous boot's owner, both for renewal and for release. The HTTP handler turns undefined into `expired: true`. The row is left in place and refresh() can still admit it until its lease_until runs out (up to 30 s). Held external leases are adopted, but waiting ones are not. The issue's restart requirement names holders, and base forgot waiters on restart anyway, so the cost is a lost queue position plus a phantom slot for at most 30 s.
opus.reason: The later commit removes the `row.owner !== this.owner && row.state !== "held"` guard, so heartbeat adopts a waiting row and release deletes it whatever its owner.

title: Idle pools run a write transaction every 250 ms

codex.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
codex.failure_scenario: Even with no work, the daemon repeatedly requests the database write lock. If another process holds that lock for an extended transaction, an unnecessary idle poll blocks the daemon's event loop and delays unrelated requests.

reproduction.output:
F3-idle {"transactionsIn10s":80,"scheduledTimers":2}
F3-lock {"idlePulseBlockedMs":602,"eventLoopCallbackRan":false}

codex.evidence: Two empty file-backed pools performed 80 transactions during 10 simulated seconds. A separate subprocess then held BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 600 ms; invoking an idle pool's scheduled callback synchronously blocked for 602 ms. HEAD unconditionally calls `this.refresh(...)` in every pulse and rearms it at 250 ms; refresh ends with `.immediate()`. Store configures `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`. Base had no database polling. This establishes unnecessary contention and transient responsiveness loss, not persisted-state damage or a demonstrated incorrect result; the contention consequence requires a prolonged write lock.
codex.reason: The later commit schedules polling only for local waiters and renewal only for owned rows, leaving idle pools without recurring transactions.

opus.criterion: the cost is cosmetic or diagnostic only
opus.failure_scenario: Even when nothing is queued, each of the daemon's two slot pools takes the database write lock four times a second. That competes with every other writer on the shared SQLite file and can block the daemon for as long as another process holds the lock.

reproduction.command: bun test $TMPDIR/adj/claims.test.ts (one idle pool with db.transaction wrapped to count calls; clock advanced 10 s in 250 ms steps)
reproduction.output: F3 transactions in 10s idle: 40

opus.evidence: The constructor arms `pulse` unconditionally every `Math.min(250, options.pollMs ?? 250)` ms, and each pulse calls refresh(), which runs `this.db.transaction(...).immediate()` (a BEGIN IMMEDIATE write transaction with a DELETE) whether or not any local waiter or owned row exists. attachSlotPools creates two such pools. The issue only asks for polling by waiters. The cost is lock contention and some latency, with no wrong result unless combined with a long stall.
opus.reason: The later commit's schedule() arms the poll timer only while local waiters are pending and the renew timer only while this owner has rows, so an idle pool runs no transactions.

title: A refusal event from a newer worker aborts the session on an older coordinator

codex.criterion: the previous release breaks on rollback
codex.failure_scenario: An implement session continues on an upgraded worker while its coordinator rolls back. When the worker refuses a full-suite command, the older coordinator rejects the notification, causing the worker to abort the session before returning its result.

reproduction.output:
head emitted: {"type":"status","text":"agent-test refused: full suite","data":{"command":"bun test --parallel=4"}}
base accepts plain status: true
head accepts refusal: true
base accepts refusal: false
base rejection: [{"code":"unrecognized_keys","keys":["data"],"path":["events",0],"message":"Unrecognized key: \"data\""}]
1 pass
0 fail

codex.evidence: The throwaway probe executes HEAD's actual runToolAgent event callback, mocking scratch allocation and the slotted-command callback, and validates its output against the schema extracted from base. It reproduces schema rejection; it does not start a coordinator or worker. At HEAD, the emitter adds `data: { command: data.command }`. Base includes status events in `z.object({ type: z.literal(type), text: z.string() }).strict()`, which rejects that field. Base's worker listener calls `AgentEvents.parse(body)` and converts the resulting exception to HTTP 400. HEAD's worker client throws CoordinatorRefusal for non-200 responses below 500 (src/workers/client.ts:529-533), and its event-upload rejection handler calls `agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort()` (line 808). Base's emitter had no refusal event carrying this incompatible field.
codex.reason: The later commit removes the data field, places the redacted command in ordinary status text, restores the original strict event schema, and updates refusal-event assertions, addressing the reproduced compatibility mechanism.

opus.criterion: the previous release breaks on rollback or a newer CLI breaks against an older daemon
opus.failure_scenario: A newer coordinator hands an implement job to a newer worker, then a deploy rolls the coordinator back while the job is still running. When the agent tries the full suite, the worker sends a refusal status event with an extra field. The older coordinator rejects that whole batch of events with HTTP 400, so the worker aborts the session and the round's implement work is lost.

reproduction.command: Copied base src/workers/agent-protocol.ts into $TMPDIR, rewriting its imports to absolute paths, then ran a bun script that safeParses {seq, events:[{type:'status', text:'agent-test refused: full suite', data:{command:'bun test --parallel=4'}}]} and a plain status event against the base and head AgentEvents schemas
reproduction.output:
base plain true 
base refused false Unrecognized key: "data"
head plain true 
head refused true

opus.evidence: Head src/pipeline/agent-executor.ts:79-86 sends `spec.onEvent({ type: "status", text: "agent-test refused: full suite", data: { command: data.command } })`. On a worker, spec.onEvent (src/workers/client.ts:860-867) pushes the event into the batch that is POSTed to /worker/agent-jobs/<id>/events. At base, the schema is `["text","thinking","stderr","status"].map(type => z.object({ type, text }).strict())`, so an unknown `data` key fails. Base src/server/workers.ts:245 calls `AgentEvents.parse(body)`, and its catch block at line 311-314 returns 400. On the worker, client.ts:808 has `void posts.catch(() => agentJobs.get(id)?.controller.abort())`, so a rejected events POST aborts the active session. Head widens the schema in src/workers/agent-protocol.ts:13-19 and the event type in src/harness/types.ts:41, so a newer coordinator accepts the event and an older one does not. Exposure needs a job that is in flight across a rollback (the worker received agentFullSuite=refuse from the newer coordinator). An older coordinator never sends that field, so freshly leased jobs are unaffected.
opus.reason: c9036d65 drops the `data` field and puts the command into the status text (`agent-test refused: full suite: ${data.command}`). It also reverts the agent-protocol schema and the AgentEvent type to base, so the event shape matches what the older coordinator accepts.

codex.failure_scenario: An operator removes a repository from worker eligibility while its landing checks are running remotely. The retry switches to the local checkout without running setup there, so an otherwise recoverable test failure blocks landing.

codex.failure_scenario: An operator switches from panel review to single review after a second panel review requests changes, then the daemon restarts during verification. The resumed run fails instead of continuing its remaining work.
